componentEvidence.note: Web snippets are illustrative translations of native components; focus-visible is a preview affordance, not evidence of React Native keyboard focus. Native assets are not replaced with synthetic artwork.

surfaceFollowup.scope: Current-source decision and secondary-surface patterns within the incumbent visual system; no new global tokens.
patterns: Today places all due card names and a localized count above Make a Decision; the wheel Today badge uses text, weight and primary surface independently of checked state.
Progress and Insights Sections start collapsed with labeled accessible disclosure; full existing details remain reachable.
Subscription Watch shows a themed next-check inset, actual totals and three preview rows; full agenda and empty-state add remain reachable.
Pause shows the amount awaiting decisions and second-updated localized deadline timers, day counts and explicit expiry; detail actions remain reachable.
Free Profile prioritizes Get full access on the existing success role with readable foreground; Reports is quieter. Premium Profile prioritizes Reports.
Settings groups preferences, preserves payday Save/Cancel and keeps choice screens reachable during a draft; payday choices have platform-sized minimum width and height.
Category selection reveals and scrolls to the editor with reduced-motion support. Save becomes primary; Add becomes secondary. Creation retains validation, premium gates and dismissal.
The user-requested legacy Open All Settings branch and duplicate Profile shell are retired; live routes remain. Shared form sheets use incumbent shapes and headings.

paywallRedesign.scope: Approved plans-row Premium offer only; incumbent global tokens and narrative retained.

Native offer metadata owns eligibility, trial duration, localized billing periods, prices and annual total; annual equivalent remains subordinate.
Large text stacks cards and secondary groups; scroll preserves all content and insight routes.
Preserve five-second dismissal, Back/backdrop, purchase/restore/manage/legal, scroll reporting and abandoned-offer handlers.

narrative.overview:
Almost should feel like a calm, credible companion at the moment a user turns an intention into action. The interface uses cool neutral grounds, bright semantic surfaces, decisive type hierarchy, and a small number of recognizable product assets. It is supportive without posing as a bank, and expressive without letting illustration compete with the task.

The visual system is native, compact, and behavior-first. Each screen presents one dominant state or action, then uses secondary cards and lightweight line icons to explain what happens next. Light, dark, and PRO are equal product modes rather than recolored afterthoughts.
keyCharacteristics: Cool neutral backgrounds with clear, bright content surfaces.
Heavy Inter numerals and titles paired with quieter explanatory text.
Semantic savings, debt, and information colors used only where meaning is stable.
Soft cards, restrained ambient depth, and platform-sized touch targets.
Existing Almost assets used as progress objects or helpers, never as unrelated decoration.

rules.name: The Semantic Destination Rule
rules.body: Green means savings and verified accumulation; red means debt payment or debt burden. Do not swap them for novelty.

rules.name: The Theme Role Rule
rules.body: Components consume semantic theme roles rather than hardcoding a light-only palette.

rules.name: The Number Leads Rule
rules.body: On money surfaces, the amount is the strongest text; its qualifier stays adjacent and subordinate.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Use sentence case for actions and labels. Uppercase is reserved for existing compact status patterns, not page hierarchy.

rules.name: The Tonal-First Rule
rules.body: Establish hierarchy with semantic surfaces and borders before adding shadow.

rules.name: The Honest Track Rule
rules.body: Progress tracks show the real clamped value; zero has no visible fill.

rules.name: The Honest Offer Rule
rules.body: Trial, billing and eligibility presentation derives from the actual native offer; no illustrative concept value becomes production subscription copy.

dos: Do use one clear focal action per state and show the real-world handoff before asking for proof.
Do reuse the semantic theme roles in light, dark, and PRO, including every configured PRO accent.
Do keep money values tabular, prominent, localized, and paired with an explicit meaning.
Do use existing Almost art when it explains progress or provides contextual help.
Do distinguish painted control size from interactive target size and show an empty track for zero progress.
Do preserve reduced motion, RTL, Dynamic Type, screen-reader labels, and native dismissal behavior.
donts: Don't propagate inherited eyebrow labels, glyph navigation icons or unassigned native display faces as new house-style rules; their presence is retained implementation debt, not authority for future surfaces.
Don't introduce a Budget action to spend; Budget has savings and debt destinations only.
Don't imply Almost holds or transfers money. The user's external bank or deposit service performs the transaction.
Don't replace product assets and semantic surfaces with random glossy fintech art, generic charts, or unrelated gradients.
Don't use illustration as filler when task state, amount, or the next action needs the space.
Don't remove, hide, or visually demote an existing flow to simplify a redesign.
